predecessors.name: Mataram Sultanate
predecessors.text: the western half of the Sultanate of Mataram given to Prince Mangkubumi with its capital in Yogyakarta (Treaty of Giyanti, 13 February 1755)

successors.name: Dutch East Indies
successors.text: the mancanagara and 'a significant part of its territory', annexed after the Java War; the rump, 'the modern boundary of the Yogyakarta Special Region', stayed under the sultan

ledger.x: 13 February 1755: the Treaty of Giyanti makes Mangkubumi Sultan Hamengkubuwono I at Yogyakarta.
1755: the sultanate is born a protectorate of the Dutch East India Company.
1799: the Company protectorate ends; the protectorate passes to the Batavian Republic.
1806: the Batavian Republic protectorate ends; the Kingdom of the Netherlands follows.
1806: protectorate of the Kingdom of the Netherlands.
1811: the Dutch protectorate lapses when Britain takes Java.
1811: protectorate of the British East India Company.
20 June 1812: British troops storm the palace.
The sack was a single action; the British then held Java until 1816 with Yogyakarta a protectorate of the East India Company.
1813: the British carve the Duchy of Pakualaman out of the sultanate.
1816: the British protectorate ends; Java returns to the Dutch.
1830: the Dutch annex the outlying lands.
1830: this dossier ends with the Dutch annexation of the mancanagara; the infobox protectorate runs on to 1942 for the rump sultanate, which is not drawn here.

wars.name: Java War
wars.outcome: Diponegoro rebelled on 21 July 1825 and was arrested at the Dutch Resident's house on 28 March 1830; afterwards the Dutch 'annexed significant proportions of the princely states' remaining territories' (the mancanagara) and the Cultivation System followed.

wars.name: British occupation of Java and sack of Yogyakarta
wars.outcome: On 20 June 1812 1,200 British troops sacked the palace, deposed Hamengkubuwono II and set up Hamengkubuwono III; in 1813 the British split Pakualaman off Yogyakarta.

certainty.note: The Giyanti line between 'eastern' and 'western' halves of Mataram, the Pakualaman enclave and the mancanagara have no boundary on the pages opened; all frontiers soft.
